newsitem.title: USA: Calif. localities added to BankAmerica lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Calif. localities added to BankAmerica lawsuit.

text.p: More than 50 local governments in California have joined San Francisco in suing BankAmerica Corp, the nation's third largest bank, for allegedly mismanaging municipal bond funds, a lead attorney in the case said on Tuesday.

San Francisco Deputy City Attorney Matt Davis told Reuters the number of plaintiffs could approach 100 by the close of business Wednesday, the deadline for local governments to join the BankAmerica lawsuit without court approval.

San Francisco and California's attorney general have sued BankAmerica unit Bank of America, alleging it overcharged issuers, failed to return unclaimed funds from bond trust accounts, and improperly invested funds from some of the accounts.
Bank of America maintains that the investments it made were appropriate, and that it has fully returned unclaimed funds from the bond accounts.
"There's nothing new in the filings," Bank of America spokesman John Keane said.

Davis said El Dorado County joined San Francisco's lawsuit along with the cities of Emeryville, Fairfield, Foster City, Gilroy, Glendale, Inglewood, Menlo Park, Pasadena, Pleasanton, Richmond, San Carlos, San Rafael, Vallejo and Ventura.

The suit also joined by the counties of Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Nevada, Riverside, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Sonoma, Solano and Tulare, as well as the cities of Belmont, Burbank, Folsom, Santa Rosa, San Bernardino and Industry.
Many local water districts and redevelopment agencies have also joined the case.

The San Francisco and state lawsuits were based on a so-called "whistleblower" complaint filed under seal in April 1995 by Patrick Stull, a former vice president for corporate trust at Bank of America.
